chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufy, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Nasr ibn Qaboos that he had heard Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:

The astrologer is cursed, the priest is cursed, the magician is cursed, the female singer is cursed, and those who give them a place to live and earn an income from their work are cursed. And he (peace be upon him) said: An astrologer is like a priest; a priest is like a magician; a magician is like an atheist and an atheist goes to Hell.

The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: What is meant by ‘an astrologer is damned’ is that the astrologer who claims that the universe has always existed, denies its Creator and doesn’t believe in the Honorable the Exalted God is damned.

key_terms.الْمُنَجِّمُ: Astrologer (specifically one claiming eternity of the spheres)

ai.seo_question: Who are the five cursed people according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these five groups under the title 'The Five Cursed Ones,' establishing a hierarchy of curse that culminates in the astrologer being equated with the disbeliever destined for Hell. The compiler’s specific definition of the 'astrologer' as one who asserts the eternity of the celestial spheres (Qadam al-Falak) while denying the Creator highlights a key theological critique of Greek cosmology within Shia scholarship. This distinction underscores that the curse is not merely on the practice of divination, but on the underlying metaphysical error of attributing independent existence to the heavens.
